summary: Build practical tourism crisis management and business continuity skills with ISO 22301, ICS, and recovery planning. Enrol today.
lede: Crisis readiness and business continuity for tourism help teams prepare for disruption and sustain essential services. Designed for professionals in tourism operations, guest services, destination management, risk and communications, the course covers business impact analysis, crisis-team activation and continuity planning, with practice in guest messaging and recovery reporting.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who already work in tourism operations, guest services, destination management, risk, or communications and need a practical framework for crisis readiness and continuity execution. Tourism Operations Managers coordinating disruption response and service continuity. Hotel Duty Managers managing guest-facing escalation and recovery procedures. Destination Resilience Officers maintaining tourism crisis registers and response plans. Tour Operator Supervisors aligning itineraries with continuity and evacuation contingencies. Resort Security Managers supporting incident escalation and site control. Guest Relations Managers drafting crisis messages and service recovery updates. Travel Risk Consultants advising on tourism disruption scenarios and mitigation. Transport Operations Coordinators protecting movement continuity during service interruption. Compliance and Risk Officers documenting incidents and continuity obligations. Marketing and Communications Leads managing reputation and stakeholder updates.
modules: Business Impact Analysis and Risk Register
prerequisites: You need a laptop, basic spreadsheet skills, and access to current tourism operating documents if available. Bring any existing crisis plans, emergency contact lists, incident logs, or continuity templates from your workplace so you can apply the exercises to realistic material.
